title: Parallel Execution and Module Critical Paths Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies parallel execution and module critical paths?
options: Expose independent graph work and reduce invalidation before tuning bounded parallel resources.
Split every package into a module
Put shared types in one frequently changed core module
questions.answer: Expose independent graph work and reduce invalidation before tuning bounded parallel resources.
questions.explanation: The correct approach preserves Gradle’s lazy model, explicit data flow, variant correctness, functional evidence and operability.

questions.prompt: A private implementation change in an implementation dependency should always recompile every consumer.
questions.explanation: Increasing org.gradle.workers.max on a memory-bound agent can make builds slower or unstable through contention and swapping.

questions.prompt: Which graph property limits the best possible parallel build time?
questions.answer: The duration of the longest dependent chain—the critical path.
questions.explanation: The answer names the model property that makes the build behaviour predictable rather than relying on incidental script order.
